caption: A ripple counter of copper bulbs wound up a spiral stair. A copper bulb flips (lit / unlit) each time its power rises; the button on bulb 0 flips it at every press. A comparator reads each bulb (15 while it is lit) into a stone, which powers that bit's output; a torch on the side of that stone is lit while the bulb is unlit and powers the next bulb, which stands on the torch: when a bulb goes out, its torch lights and flips the next bulb, so each bit flips when the bit below it goes from 1 to 0 (counting up). Each comparator stands on the stone of the stage below; only the first needs a floor.

A ripple counter of copper bulbs. A copper bulb flips (lit / unlit) each time its power rises. The button on bulb 0 flips it at every press. A comparator reads each bulb (15 while it is lit) into a stone, which powers that bit's output; a torch on that stone is lit while the bulb is unlit and powers the next bulb: when a bulb goes out, its torch lights and flips the next bulb, so each bit flips when the bit below it goes from 1 to 0 (counting up).

A torch hung on each input gives its opposite. One wire touches both torches: it carries "a0 or a1 is off", at full strength beside a lit torch and one level weaker a block away. Comparators in subtract mode each read an input or an opposite at the back and a wire at a side, and an output stays lit only while its comparator's side is weaker than its back, so exactly one of the four outputs is lit for each pair of inputs. (w86, 2026-10-21, `circuit arith synth --r7`.)
